questions.q: A particle executes S.H.M. of amplitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> along <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis. At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, the position of the particle is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> and it moves along positive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis. The displacement of particle in time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mo> </mo><mi>sin</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi><mo> </mo><mo>+</mo><mo> </mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>, then the value <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>δ</mi></math> will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

f(x)=exsinx

We know that the slope of tangent is given by dydx=f'x.

Now,

f'(x)=Z=exsinx+excosx

Z=exsinx+cosx

dZdx=exsinx+cosx+excosx-sinx

⇒dZdx=2excosx

For maxima, dZdx=0

⇒2excosx=0

⇒excosx=0

∵ex≠0, x∈R 

∴cosx=0⇒x=π2, 3π2; ∵x∈0,2π 

Now, 

⇒d2Zdx2=2excosx-2exsinx

                 =2excosx-sinx

d2Zdx2x=π2=-2eπ2<0→MAXIMA

And, d2Zdx2x=3π2=2e3π2>0→MINIMA

Hence, Z=dydxslope of tangent is maximum when x=π2.

questions.q: The time period of oscillation of a simple pendulum of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi></math> suspended from the roof of a vehicle, which moves without friction down an inclined plane of inclination <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math>, is given by :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration of vehicle down the incline will be a=gsinα
In the frame of the vehicle, we have to apply pseudo force. The Force diagram is shown in figure.
Component of mg along the inclined (i.e. mgsinα) will balance the pseudo force. Therefore, geff=gcosα


Hence,

T=2πLgeff=2πLgcosα.

questions.q: A pendulum is executing simple harmonic motion and its maximum kinetic energy is $\mathrm{K}_{1}$. If the length of the pendulum is doubled and it performs simple harmonic motion with the same amplitude as in the first case, its maximum kinetic energy is $\mathrm{K}_{2}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$K=\frac{1}{2} m \omega^{2} x^{2}\Rightarrow K_{\max }=\frac{1}{2} m \omega^{2} A^{2}$

A $=L \theta\omega=\sqrt{\frac{g}{L}}\Rightarrow K=\frac{1}{2} m \cdot \frac{g}{L} \cdot L^{2} \theta^{2}=\frac{1}{2} m g L \theta^{2}\therefore \frac{K_{1}}{K_{2}}=\frac{L}{2 L}=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow K_{2}=2 K_{1}\therefore \frac{\mathrm{K}_{1}}{\mathrm{~K}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{L}}{2 \mathrm{~L}}=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{K}_{2}=2 \mathrm{~K}_{1}$

questions.q: The point A moves with a uniform speed along the circumference of a circle of radius 0.36 m and covers 30° in 0.1 s. The perpendicular projection P from A on the diameter MN represents the simple harmonic motion of P. The restoration force per unit mass when P touches M will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The point A covers 30° in 0.1 s.
Then, we have π6 rad⟶0.1 s.
Or 1 rad⟶0.1π6 s
Or 2π in→ 0.1×6π×2π
Thus, time taken is T=1.2 sec.

We know that ω=2πT
Then, ω=2π1.2
Restoration force (F)=mω2A.

Then Restoration force per unit mass Fm=ω2 A
Fm=2π1.22×0.36

≅9.87 N

questions.q:
A particle is subjected two simple harmonic motions as :
$\mathrm{x}_1=\sqrt{7} \sin 5 \mathrm{tcm}$
and $x_2=2 \sqrt{7} \sin \left(5 t+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \mathrm{cm}$
where x is displacement and $t$ is time in seconds. The maximum acceleration of the particle is $\mathrm{x} \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$. The value of x is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}_1=\sqrt{7} \sin 5 \mathrm{t} \\ & \mathrm{x}_2=2 \sqrt{7} \sin \left(5 \mathrm{t}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\end{aligned}$
From phasor,

$\therefore$ Amplitude of resultant $\mathrm{SHM}=7$
$\begin{aligned} & \phi=\tan ^{-1} \frac{2 \sqrt{7} \times \sqrt{3} / 2}{\sqrt{7}+2 \sqrt{7} \times \frac{1}{2}}=\tan ^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{21}}{2 \sqrt{7}}=\tan ^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ & \therefore \quad \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{R}}=7 \sin (5 \mathrm{t}+\phi) \\ & \quad \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{R}}=-7 \times 25 \sin (5 \mathrm{t}+\phi) \\ & \therefore \mathrm{a}_{\max }=175 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{sec}=175 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{sec}\end{aligned}$

From given condition, A02=A0e-0.1×t
⇒ln2=0.1×t
t=ln20.1=0.6930.10=6.935≈7 s

questions.q: Choose the correct length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>)</mo></math> versus square of time period <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></math> ) graph for a simple pendulum executing simple harmonic motion.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
A simple pendulum consists of a point mass attached to an inextensible string and suspended from a support.

The formula to calculate the time period T of a simple pendulum is given by

T=2πlg.......................(1)

where, l is the length of the pendulum and g is the acceleration due to gravity.

Simplify equation (1) to obtain the relation between the time period and the length.

T2=4π2g×𝓁T2∝l............................(2)

Equation (2) suggests that the graph between the square of the time period versus the length of the pendulum is a straight line passing through the origin.

questions.q: In figure (A), mass 2m is fixed on mass m which is attached to two springs of spring constant k. In figure (B), mass m is attached to two spring of spring constant k and 2k. If mass m in (A) and (B) are displaced by distance x horizontally and then released, then time period T1 and T2 corresponding to (A) and (B) respectively follow the relation.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The time period of spring block system is given by T=2πmk.

In both the cases springs are connected in parallel,

In case 1: keq=2k and total mass is 3m. Therefore,

 T1=2π3mkeq=2π3m2k

In case 2: keq=3k and total mass is m. Therefore,

T2=2πm3k

⇒T1T2=92=32

questions.q: Which graph represents the difference between total energy and potential energy of a particle executing SHM vs its distance from mean position?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In a SHM, mechanical energy is conserved. So, the sum of kinetic energy and potential energy remains constant.

For a SHM,

T.E.-U=K.E

⇒T.E.-U=12mv2=12mω2A2-x2

This is the equation of a downward parabola.

questions.solution:
$x(t)=x_0 \sin ^2\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)=\frac{x_0}{2}(1-\cos t)$
Clearly $\frac{x_0}{2}$ is mean position.

questions.q: Two simple pendulums having lengths $l_1$ and $l_2$ with negligible string mass undergo angular displacements $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$, from their mean positions, respectively. If the angular accelerations of both pendulums are same, then which expression is correct?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \omega=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\ell}} \\ & \alpha=-\omega^2 \theta \\ & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{~g}}{\ell_1} \theta_1=\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\ell_2} \theta_2 \\ & \Rightarrow \theta_1 \ell_2=\theta_2 \ell_2\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A simple pendulum is placed at a place where its distance from the earth's surface is equal to the radius of the earth. If the length of the string is 4 m, then the time period of small oscillations will be _________s.

[take g=π2 m s-2]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at surface of earth, g=GMR2.

Now, at distance R from the surface of the earth, g'=GMR+R2=g4

Therefore,
T=2πlg4

⇒T=2π4×4 g

⇒T=2π4π=8 s

questions.q: At a given point of time the value of displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is given as y=A cos30°. If amplitude is 40 cm and kinetic energy at that time is 200 J, the value of force constant 1.0×10x N m–1. The value of x is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the kinetic energy K of a particle executing SHM is given by

K=12kA2-y2   ...1

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the value of the unknown parameter.

K=12×k×A2-A2cos230°= 12×k×A2sin230°⇒200=12×1.0×10x×0.42×122= 2×10x100⇒102=10x-2⇒x-2=2⇒x=4
